rules.quote: Use sentence case – capitalise only the first letter of the title and the first letter of any proper noun.

rules.why: G-1: whole-work title formatting is a distinct check.

rules.quote: Use quotation marks for the titles of chapters, poems or sections.
rules.violation_condition: A chapter, poem or section title from a classic is not enclosed in quotation marks in a reference or in-text citation.
when: Applies to titles of chapters, poems or sections in references and in-text citations.

covers.quote: List classics with other references

You don’t usually need a reference list for classics.

rules.quote: If you’re using a reference list, include any classics that you cite.
rules.violation_condition: A document has a reference list but omits a classic cited in the document from that list.
when: Applies when the document uses a reference list.
A reference list is not usually required solely for classics.
rules.why: G-2, G-3 and G-4: consolidate repeated inclusion instructions and retain the permission not to have a reference list.

rules.quote: Include the information that you know in in-text citations.
rules.specification: The page does not enumerate the information required by this general instruction. The writer’s knowledge cannot be established from the citation alone.
rules.violation_condition: An in-text citation omits identifying information about the classic that is known to the writer.
when: Applies to in-text citations of classics.
Information such as the author or original publication date may be unavailable.
rules.why: Retain an explicit requirement about citation content, but do not invent required fields or assume the writer knows them.
